name: Sailback
author: James Wyatt
section: An Ixalan Bestiary, Teeth and Frills
appearanceEvidence: Dan Scott's Snapping Sailback on p. 30 shows the long, toothed snout, dark blue scales, colored head quills, and tall orange-to-blue sail. The full body and subdued palette are editorial choices for the new portrait.
habitatEvidence: p. 30 describes Sailbacks as predators that ambush prey in lakes and rivers.
secondaryCrossCheck: Compared against the corresponding Monster Manual entry in the local 5etools extract. The Ixalan , Monster Manual print witness, and Wizards rules determine the staged block.
creditedArt: Dan Scott, Snapping Sailback. Retain the existing book image and credit.

name: Swarm of Piranhas
author: James Wyatt
section: An Ixalan Bestiary, Life of the Waters
appearanceEvidence: p. 40 describes small biting fish gathering in churning swarms. Silver-grey scales, red bellies, body shape, and forked tails are editorial portrait details based on a recognizable piranha silhouette.
habitatEvidence: p. 40 names the Great River and its tributaries. Freshwater is an editorial normalization of those habitats. Underwater follows the inherited Water Breathing trait.
secondaryCrossCheck: Compared against the corresponding Monster Manual entry in the local 5etools extract. The Ixalan , Monster Manual print witness, and Wizards rules determine the staged block.
errataEvidence: Version 1.1 adds immunity to the grappled condition for all swarms. This correction predates the first printing of Plane Shift: Ixalan.

name: Trilobite
author: James Wyatt
section: An Ixalan Bestiary, Life of the Waters
appearanceEvidence: YW Tang's Shore Keeper on p. 40 shows a dark, broad, segmented marine arthropod with rust-red extensions. The three-lobed shell layout and compound eyes are editorial identification details. Both catalog sizes share the portrait.
habitatEvidence: p. 40 places trilobites along the shores of rivers and seas. Beaches, riverbanks, and shallow water are search terms drawn from its nearby shoreline description.
secondaryCrossCheck: Compared against the corresponding Monster Manual entry in the local 5etools extract. The Ixalan , Monster Manual print witness, and Wizards rules determine the staged block.

name: Tyrant
author: James Wyatt
appearanceEvidence: The Dinosaur Tyrants text on p. 31 describes the oversized head, blade-like teeth, and reduced forelimbs. Jonathan Kuo's Regisaur Alpha on that page also informs the palette and feathering. The staged portrait uses a new pose for an ordinary wild tyrant.
habitatEvidence: Editorial setting tags inferred from the Dinosaur Tyrants section and the forested terrain in the Regisaur Alpha illustration, p. 31. The printed action block has no formal habitat list.
